skill.description: Guides Dart and Flutter projects through compiling, linking, packaging, and verifying C or C++ libraries with Native Assets hooks.
skill.summary: Configure Dart Native Assets hooks for local C builds, remote binaries, FFI bindings, and linker tree-shaking.
skill.author: flutter

security_audit.summary: The analyzer mostly misclassified Markdown backticks and ordinary Dart entry points as command execution or reconnaissance. The remote native-library download is confirmed, and the documented MD5 validation creates a separate integrity weakness. Privileged package installation is explicit and fixed, while certificate and Python HTTP alerts are unrelated text matches.

remediation.issue: Downloaded native libraries are validated with MD5 in the example.
remediation.suggestion: Require SHA-256 or stronger digests from a trusted manifest, pin immutable releases, and delete downloaded files after any validation failure.

remediation.issue: Build hooks depend on remotely hosted native executables.
remediation.suggestion: Document the host trust boundary, restrict approved origins, enforce download limits and timeouts, and retain the verified local-build fallback.

content.user_title: Build Dart Native Assets with FFI Hooks
content.value_statement: Native C and C++ integration in Dart requires platform-aware build, link, and packaging hooks. This skill guides local compilation, verified binary downloads, and linker tree-shaking.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to place Dart build and link hooks in a package.
Shows local C library compilation through native_toolchain_c APIs.
Demonstrates FFIgen record-use mappings for native symbol tree-shaking.
Compares local compilation with downloading precompiled libraries.
Shows platform-specific CodeAsset registration for bundled dynamic libraries.
Provides checks for outputs, exports, tree-shaking, and offline builds.
limitations: Requires a compatible C compiler for the local build approach.
Provides illustrative package versions, URLs, hashes, and paths that require project-specific replacement.
Does not generate production binaries or release infrastructure.
Covers dynamic native libraries more fully than static library workflows.

use_cases.title: Add Native Code to a Dart Package
use_cases.description: Create build hooks that compile included C sources and register the resulting library as a Dart Code Asset.

use_cases.title: Package Native Libraries for Flutter
use_cases.description: Prepare platform-specific dynamic libraries for automatic bundling across macOS, Linux, and Windows.

use_cases.title: Reduce Native Binary Size
use_cases.description: Connect FFIgen usage records to a link hook that removes unreferenced native symbols.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Build Hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a Dart Native Assets build hook for my C sources. Use native_toolchain_c and explain every required file.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner is adding one C library to a Dart package.

prompt_templates.title: Add FFI Bindings
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate FFIgen bindings with my Native Assets setup. Include the shared library specification and platform export requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: A package already contains C sources but lacks generated Dart bindings.

prompt_templates.title: Package Precompiled Libraries
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a build hook that downloads platform-specific native libraries, verifies SHA-256 hashes, and supports an offline local-build fallback.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team distributes trusted release binaries to avoid local compilation.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Native Tree-Shaking
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a link hook using record_use mappings and native_toolchain_c tree-shaking. Include tests for retained and removed symbols.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced package needs smaller production binaries and verified exports.

output_examples.input: Set up local compilation for a bundled SQLite source file.
output: A dependency list for hooks, code assets, native toolchains, record use, and FFIgen.
A shared C library specification used by both build and link phases.
A verification checklist covering tests and platform library outputs.

output_examples.input: Use precompiled libraries while preserving offline development.
output: A platform-aware download design with immutable release locations and SHA-256 verification.
A local_build switch that compiles included sources when network access is unavailable.
Clear failure behavior for unsupported targets and integrity mismatches.

output_examples.input: Remove unused native symbols from a release build.
output: A link-hook design that maps recorded Dart calls to native symbol names.
Platform-specific export inspection steps for macOS, Linux, and Windows.

best_practices: Resolve package paths with Uri APIs and keep hooks platform-independent.
Use SHA-256 or stronger digests for every downloaded native binary.
Test local, offline, unsupported-platform, and symbol-stripping paths in continuous integration.
anti_patterns: Do not invoke compilers through dynamically constructed shell commands.
Do not download or register native binaries before verifying their source and digest.
Do not hardcode generated output directories or host-specific absolute paths.

faq.question: Does this skill require a local compiler?
faq.answer: Local compilation requires Xcode tools, GCC, Clang, or MSVC. Precompiled downloads can avoid that requirement.

faq.question: Which Dart packages does the guidance use?
faq.answer: It uses hooks, code_assets, native_toolchain_c, record_use, and FFIgen for build, link, packaging, and binding tasks.

faq.question: Can it support offline development?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented local_build option uses included sources and an installed compiler without downloading binaries.

faq.question: How are downloaded libraries validated?
faq.answer: The skill demonstrates digest validation. Production projects should replace illustrative MD5 values with trusted SHA-256 or stronger digests.

faq.question: Does it support native symbol tree-shaking?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps recorded Dart FFI method use to native symbols and passes those symbols to linker tree-shaking.

faq.question: Which desktop platforms are covered?
faq.answer: The examples cover macOS dynamic libraries, Linux shared objects, and Windows DLL files.
